plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Rosy-lilac, goblet-shaped flowers push straight out of bare ground with no leaves, as if a spring crocus had lost its way. Whole meadows can turn soft pink as the days shorten.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn, typically late August through October
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges of central and western Europe, including the UK, Germany and France
plants.funFact: Despite the name, this is not a true crocus. It belongs to the lily relatives and produces colchicine, a potent toxin that is also used in medicine. Its leaves appear in spring, long after the flowers have faded.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks carry huge golden faces that follow the sun across the sky. In early September, fields in the Northern Hemisphere glow with late-season blooms as seed heads begin to ripen.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer into early autumn, with peak bloom from July to September
plants.location: Fields and gardens across the temperate Northern Hemisphere, including the central United States, southern France and Ukraine
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not one flower but hundreds of tiny florets. Their seeds are arranged in spirals that follow Fibonacci numbers.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Fluffy, fragrant golden pom-poms cover the branches in a dazzling display. In early spring they brighten the bushland of southeastern Australia.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring, roughly July to October, peaking around August and September
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, at the start of the Southern Hemisphere spring.
